subject: Handoff: on-prem networking modules for Acme Health — module handoff & QA
content:
From: Alex Burns <alex.burns@acmehealth.io>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Handoff: on-prem networking modules for Acme Health — module handoff & QA

Hi Chloe / Diego / Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week. Acme Health is ready for the next step: a controlled handoff of the Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules for our on-prem VPC build so we can run an internal QA pass before production cutover. A few asks from our side:

- Confirm module ownership and who will be the on-call contact during our QA window (next Tues/Wed).
- Provide a short QA checklist you recommend to validate network isolation, BGP peering config, and DNS routing between racks.
- Provide the audit artifacts we need for our SOC2 evidence (module change log, network diagrams, and any secret-policy changes).

Attachments: network-topology.png (diagram), module-change-log.md (changelog).

We have a JIRA ticket tracking this: INFRA-4123.

Can we schedule a 30-min handoff today or tomorrow? Prefer late morning PST.

—Alex
Alex Burns
Sr. Cloud Engineer, Acme Health
alex.burns@acmehealth.io

-----
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Burns <alex.burns@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: on-prem networking modules for Acme Health — module handoff & QA

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- Ownership: Redwood Infra (Chloe Martin) owns module releases; Diego Fernandez is the module maintainer and primary technical contact. Markus Klein will be on-call for release-day rollbacks. Irene will own the SOC2 artifact bundle.
- QA checklist: see inline below.
- Audit artifacts: attaching module-change-log.md and the network diagram you shared; we will also attach terraform-secrets-policy.patch after internal review.

Proposed QA checklist (quick):
1) Module unit tests pass (terraform validate + tflint)
2) Plan review against `acme-prod` workspace; no drift on existing BGP sessions
3) BGP neighbor reachability test (control-plane) — confirm ASNs and prefixes
4) DNS resolution tests across racks (internal DNS and split-horizon)
5) Helm chart smoke (ingress + certs) in staging cluster
6) Ansible idempotence run for config rendering on a test rack
7) Secrets & policies: validate KMS reference and no plaintext credentials in state

Schedule: I can run the handoff at 11:30 AM PST today for 30 min — demo + runbook walkthrough. If that works for your team I’ll send an invite.

Attachments: [attachment: module-change-log.md], [attachment: network-topology.png]

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.ai

On Mon, Mar 9, 2026 at 10:22 AM Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Alex / Chloe — a couple of technical notes before the handoff:
>
> 1) Terraform modules: we introduced a variable `enable_bgp_md5` in `redwood_network/bgp` to toggle MD5 auth for BGP sessions. Default is false to match current Acme staging config. If you require MD5 on prod we can flip, but we need to coordinate AS prep.
>
> 2) Helm: ingress controller values have a new `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` default which preserves source IPs. This impacts load-balancer behavior; test plan should include full e2e TCP tests.
>
> 3) Secrets: attaching a proposed patch that adds an explicit `kms_key_alias` reference rather than using inline keys. It also contains a short pre-apply check to validate KMS access: see terraform-secrets-policy.patch (attached).
>
> Quick inline sample for your ops team (terraform):
>
>```hcl
>resource "aws_vpn_connection" "acme_edge" {
>  count = var.edge_enabled ? 1 : 0
>  customer_gateway_id = var.customer_gateway_id
>  transit_gateway_id  = var.transit_gateway_id
>  static_routes_only  = false
>  tags = {
>    Name = "acme-edge-connection"
>  }
>}
>```
>
> I’ll bring this sample into the handoff deck and we can walk through the variants. I’ve linked the JIRA INFRA-4123 to the change set.
>
> —Diego

On Mon, Mar 9, 2026 at 11:35 AM Alex Burns <alex.burns@acmehealth.io> wrote:
> Chloe / Diego — 11:30 works for me. Thanks for the checklist, Diego — the MD5 toggle is expected in prod for our edge peering. Please ensure the handoff includes the exact terraform plan command and the expected plan output snippet we should see (so our procurement team can sign off).
>
> Also, for SOC2 we will need a short artifact that shows: module owner, change history, and who approved the last change (we prefer structured metadata). If Irene can produce that bundle after the handoff that will cover our evidence request.
>
> Can you also confirm whether any helm values change requires a storage migration (we want to avoid any PV interruptions during the cutover).
>
> Thanks — see you at 11:30.
>
> —Alex

-----
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Burns <alex.burns@acmehealth.io>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Handoff: on-prem networking modules for Acme Health — module handoff & QA

Alex / team — following up from the handoff: thanks for the session. Per the SOC2 request I’ve packaged the artifacts you need:

- module-change-log.md (attached) — includes author, timestamp, and PR link for last 12 changes
- network-topology.png — final diagram used in the demo
- terraform-secrets-policy.patch — shows the KMS alias change and a pre-apply check script

I’ve added structured metadata to the changelog: `owner: chloe_martin`, `approver: diego_fernandez`, `release_tag: acme-2026-03-09`. I’ll upload the bundle to the shared Drive folder (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3INFRA) and attach the JIRA ticket INFRA-4123 for evidence tracking.

Next steps:
- Chloe/Diego: schedule a short runbook validation with Acme ops for the production preflight (we agreed on a 2-hour window).
- Markus: be on-call during initial apply for first 24 hours.
- I will create a SOC2 evidence card in our tracker and notify Acme procurement.

If you need any additional fields in the changelog let me know; otherwise I’ll mark this JIRA task as "evidence_ready".

—Irene
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
